## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

{"number":1188,"title":"Nothing prunes an absorbed pack's leftover directory from a member's mount","body":"Blocked-by: #1187

Model: opus

When a pack is **absorbed** into another (`chrome-extension-release` → `chrome-extension`, `github-actions` → `git-github`, `firebase-release` → `firebase` — #1057, #1079), its directory stays in every member's mount forever. The pack flow "replaces a declared pack's tree wholesale but never removes a tree that has stopped being declared" (`engine/migrations/2026-08-19-pack-renames/migration.mjs`), and no migration record covers the absorptions — grep finds none.

After #1187 those leftovers are inert rather than fatal, so this is dead weight, not breakage: a complete, loadable copy of a retired pack sitting beside its survivor in seven members' trees.

**Why a rename record doesn't fit.** The rename records work by `aliases`, which *move* the legacy directory onto the canonical path, and depend on "the canonical side does not exist yet" — for an absorption the survivor's directory is already there, so the move cannot apply. The action here is a **delete**, which the record vocabulary has no shape for today.

**Done looks like**: a member's converge removes `.claudinite/shared/packs//` for each absorbed pack, and a member that already converged past the record still gets there. Confirm against a real member tree, not only a fixture — the same way #1186 was confirmed.

**Ruled out**: doing it inside #1187. That change unfreezes the fleet and stays scoped to the loader; a destructive sweep over members' trees is a separate concern with its own risk.

Worth checking while here whether the absorbed ids can start coming out of `RENAMED_PACKS` — its own retirement rule is "no member's declaration and no member's stamped `packVersions` still carries that spelling", which several members still do.

{"number":1187,"title":"Resolve a canon pack's id against its whole tree, unfreezing seven stalled members","body":"Closes #1186

Seven members have not landed a mount update since ~10 August. Each runs its converge daily, opens a PR, and the PR is parked:

> **needs-human** — the converged tree FAILED its self-test — the machinery that runs the rules is not intact

## The bug

`RENAMED_PACKS` holds two shapes that read identically in the map:

| shape | what the tree holds |
|---|---|
| **rename** (`core` → `claudinite-lifecycle`) | one directory — the migration record's `aliases` moves it |
| **absorption** (`github-actions` → `git-github`, #1057/#1079) | **both** directories — there is no record, and the pack flow "never removes a tree that has stopped being declared" (its own words, `2026-08-19-pack-renames/migration.mjs`) |

`scanPackDir` canonicalized a canon pack's own id from the map alone. Correct for a rename; for an absorption it put two live directories on one id, so the collision guard dropped **both**:

```
pack id "chrome-extension" is declared twice — by the canon and the canon
pack id "git-github" is declared twice — by the canon and the canon
```

That fails the `pack-manifests` probe → the converged tree fails its self-test → the converge parks its own PR. The leftover directory is only ever removed by a converge that lands, so the member re-derives the same broken tree every day. A closed loop.

It surfaced on 10 August because members' current `main` runs the older engine, which does not canonicalize a canon pack's own id — so `main` self-tests clean while the branch fails, which is why the members look healthy: green runs, green `main`, nothing merging.

## The change

The map can't distinguish the two shapes, but the tree can. The id is now resolved once the whole canon scan is known: an absorbed leftover whose survivor is present keeps its own id and goes inert — what an id nothing declares is meant to do. A member still declaring the absorbed spelling is unaffected, since the declaration side resolves onto the survivor, which is live.

## Verification

Against `missingbulb/CrosswordChat`#249's **actual head**, with only this change vendored in:

```
before   Claudinite self-test: 1 of 6 probes FAILED — pack-manifests
         2 pack(s) failed to load or validate
after    Claudinite self-test: 6 probes passed.          (discoverPacks: 0 errors)
```

- New `engine-tests/pack_loader/renamed-packs.test.mjs` — 4 tests covering both shapes and the no-duplicates property; written first and watched fail on the missing export.
- Full suite: 2503 pass, 1 fail — `engine-pack-lane-shims`, which is the shallow-clone guard firing on this session's own checkout (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` → `true`). It walks pack history and touches nothing in this diff.
- `check_the_work` and `check_the_world`: 0 blocking.

**This reaches the frozen members with no per-repo hand-running** — the self-test runs against the converged tree, so the next converge vendors the fixed loader and the probe passes.

## Folders touched

**`engine/pack_loader/`** — `renamed-packs.mjs` gains `canonicalPackIdAmong`, which only maps an id forward when the target isn't already present in the tree; `pack-registry.mjs` carries each canon pack's raw id through `scanPackDir` and re-resolves the whole set in `discoverPacks`, where the full tree is known.

## Not in this change

The absorbed leftovers stay on disk as inert, undeclared trees — harmless now, but dead weight that nothing prunes. Worth its own issue (the fix is a migration record that *deletes* rather than moves, since the survivor's directory already exists); deliberately kept out of the change that unfreezes the fleet.

each absorbed pack (`chrome-extension-release`, `github-actions`,
`firebase-release`), via a new migration-record delete op — reasoning that the
pack flow "replaces a declared pack's tree wholesale but never removes a tree
that has stopped being declared."

## What I found

That reasoning is true of the *general* pack flow, but the absorption case
already has its own mechanism: `legacySpellingsOf` in
`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/pack-update.mjs` (added alongside the
original collapse in #1081) sweeps every `RENAMED_PACKS` legacy spelling —
renames and absorptions alike, since the map represents both shapes the same
way — whenever a pack update lays down its survivor's directory. It was
written for exactly this problem and, per its own test coverage, was only ever
pinned for the pure-rename shape (`core` → `claudinite-lifecycle`), not for an
absorption where the leftover sits *beside* its survivor rather than alone.

I confirmed this empirically against real members rather than only a fixture,
the same way #1186 was confirmed: I cloned all seven repos #1186 found frozen
(CrosswordChat, GoogleCalendarEventCreator, TLDR, EdFringeNow, LaughCounter,
ClaudiniteWebsite, MissingBulbWebsite). Every one converged today
(2026-08-24) once #1187 unfroze the fleet, and none carries a leftover
absorbed-pack directory or a legacy spelling in its declaration or stamped
`packVersions` anymore. The existing sweep already did the job as soon as a
converge could land.

## What this PR does

No production code change — the composed rules already produce the right
answer, so adding a new migration-record delete op would be redundant
machinery duplicating what already works. Per this repo's own rule for this
exact situation ("if they do [produce the right answer], add no production
code: pin it with a regression test that asserts the contrast case too"), I
added one test to `engine-tests/pack-update.test.mjs`, mirroring the existing
rename test but for a real absorption (`chrome-extension-release` →
`chrome-extension`): it plants the leftover directory, runs `packUpdate`, and
asserts both that the leftover is swept *and* that the converged tree
self-tests clean (the contrast case — #1186's actual failure mode). I verified
the test is not vacuous by temporarily disabling the sweep and watching it
fail, then restored the source.

## Not in this change

The issue also flagged, as a secondary "worth checking" item, whether the
absorbed ids can now come out of `RENAMED_PACKS` (its retirement rule: no
member's declaration or stamped `packVersions` still carries the old
spelling). The seven members above are clean, but I don't have a canonical
fleet-wide member list to check exhaustively, so I left the map untouched
rather than guess at full-fleet coverage.

1	// APPLYING a status transition — the write half of the vocabulary whose read half
2	// is `work-item.mjs`'s decode (tasks-dispatch DESIGN §4, the migration of #1119).
3	//
4	// One rule, and it is why this is not a plain `swapLabel`: the item may wear ANY
5	// engine version's spelling of the status it is leaving. A member's items outlive
6	// its converges, so an item filed as `task:ready` is picked up by an engine that
7	// writes `task:status:waiting-for-executor`, and a swap that named one spelling
8	// would leave the other standing — an item wearing two live statuses, which is the
9	// torn state the janitor exists to repair.
10	//
11	// Writes stay granular (add and remove named labels, never a set-write): with
12	// several executors and a scheduler run moving labels at once, a set-write from a
13	// stale snapshot clobbers a concurrent transition (DESIGN §4).
14	// The removes are UNCONDITIONAL — every spelling of the status being left, not
15	// only the ones the caller's snapshot shows. A caller holds the labels it read
16	// before its own earlier transitions, so filtering on that snapshot would skip
17	// exactly the label this engine just wrote; removing a label an issue does not
18	// carry 404s, which is the end state asked for and therefore success.
19	import { spellingsOf } from './work-item.mjs';
20	
21	// Move `item` out of `fromStatus` (canonical — every spelling of it goes) and into
22	// the label `to`, which is whatever spelling this engine writes.
23	export async function swapStatus(api, gh, repo, item, fromStatus, to) {
24	  await clearStatus(api, gh, repo, item, fromStatus);
25	  return api.addLabel(gh, repo, item.number, to);
26	}
27	
28	// Leave a status without entering another — the close path, where the terminal
29	// label is applied separately.
30	export async function clearStatus(api, gh, repo, item, status) {
31	  for (const label of spellingsOf(status)) {
32	    await api.removeLabel(gh, repo, item.number, label);
33	  }
34	}
